title: Multiplying near a round number
objectives: Multiply by 9, 98 or 99 by rounding up, then taking off whole lots
Multiply by 5 and 25 by going to 10 or 100, then halving
Pay back the gap times the other number, never the gap alone

screens.prose: Zetamac asks $7 \times 99$. Picture a rectangle 7 tall and 100 wide, with a thin strip 1 wide cut off the end.

state.caption: The hatched strip is cut away

screens.question: What is 7 × 99?

hints.text: The hatched strip is 7 tall and 1 wide.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the whole 7 by 100, then take off the strip.

byKey.one-not-lot: You took 1 off 700. The strip is 7 by 1, so take off 7.
byKey.no-adjust: That is 7 × 100. The strip of 7 still has to come off.
byKey.added: You added the strip. It is cut away, so subtract it.

explain.text: The whole rectangle is $7 \times 100 = 700$. The strip cut away is $7 \times 1 = 7$. So $7 \times 99 = 700 - 7 = 693$.

screens.prose: Drag the point along the line to choose what multiplies 7. The arrow shows the gap to 100, and the caption turns it into lots of 7.
screens.question: Drag the point to 97, then type 7 × 97.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 97 is 3 short of 100, so take three lots of 7 off 700.

byKey.one-not-lot: You took 3 off 700. 97 is three lots of 7 short, so take off 21.
byKey.one-lot: That is 7 × 99. 97 is three short of 100, so three lots of 7 come off.
byKey.added: You added three lots. 97 is below 100, so they come off.
byKey.no-adjust: That is 7 × 100. Three lots of 7 still have to come off.

explain.text: 97 is 3 short of 100, so $7 \times 97$ is three lots of 7 short of 700. That is $700 - 21 = 679$. The further from 100, the more lots you pay back.

screens.prose: You rounded up to 100, then paid back the gap in whole lots. That is **compensating**. It works near 10 too: $9 \times 46$ is ten lots of 46, less one lot.
screens.question: What is 9 × 46?

hints.text: The hatched strip is one lot of 46.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out ten lots of 46, then take off one lot.

byKey.minus-nine: You took 9 off 460. Ten lots minus one lot means taking off 46.
byKey.one-not-lot: You took 1 off 460. One lot here is a whole 46.
byKey.added: You added a lot of 46. 9 is one less than 10, so take it off.
byKey.no-adjust: That is 10 × 46. One lot of 46 still has to come off.

explain.text: $10 \times 46 = 460$, and one lot of 46 comes off. $460 - 46 = 414$. This is the nines pattern from the tables, now on any number.

screens.prose: Five is half of ten. Here is ten lots of 68, cut in half.
screens.question: What is 5 × 68?

hints.text: The shaded half is 5 lots of 68.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find ten lots of 68, then halve it.

byKey.no-halve: That is ten lots of 68. Five lots is half of it.
byKey.lost-zero: You halved 68 but skipped the ten lots. Half of 680 is 340.
byKey.extra-zero: You went to 100 lots. Five is half of ten, so halve 680.

explain.text: $10 \times 68 = 680$, and half of that is 340. Halving a round number is quicker than adding five lots of 68. The same move gives $50 \times 68$ as half of 6800.

screens.prose: 25 is a quarter of 100. So 25 lots are a quarter of 100 lots: halve, then halve again.
screens.question: What is 7 × 25?

hints.text: The shaded quarter is 25 lots of 7.
700 halved is 350. Halved again, it is 175.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find 100 lots of 7, then halve twice.

byKey.halved-once: You halved once, which gives 50 lots. Halve again for 25 lots.
byKey.no-quarter: That is 100 lots of 7. 25 lots is a quarter of it.
byKey.went-to-ten: You started from 10 lots, not 100. A quarter of 700 is 175.

explain.text: $100 \times 7 = 700$. Half is 350, and half again is 175. Two halvings make a quarter, so $7 \times 25 = 175$.

screens.prose: The same move runs the other way. Four lots is two lots, doubled. Each strip here is one lot of 87.
screens.question: What is 4 × 87?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Double 87, then double the result.

byKey.doubled-once: That is two lots of 87. Double once more for four lots.
byKey.doubled-three: You doubled three times, which is eight lots. Four lots needs two doublings.

explain.text: Two strips make $2 \times 87 = 174$, and all four make $2 \times 174 = 348$. Doubling twice is times 4, and halving twice is a quarter. Both beat counting up in lots.

screens.prose: Sam rounds $8 \times 98$ up to $8 \times 100 = 800$, then takes off 2, because 98 is 2 below 100. Sam gets 798.

state.caption: The hatched strip is cut away

screens.question: Is Sam right?

options.text: No. Two lots of 8 come off, so it is 784
Yes. 98 is 2 below 100, so take 2 off 800
options.why: You agreed with Sam, who took off the gap of 2. The strip cut away is 8 by 2, so 16 comes off.

options.text: No. One lot of 8 comes off, so it is 792
options.why: You took off one 8. 98 is two short of 100, so two lots of 8 come off.

options.text: No. Two lots of 8 go on, so it is 816
options.why: You added the strip. 98 is below 100, so the strip is cut away.

hints.text: How big is the hatched strip?
The strip is 8 tall and 2 wide.

feedback.correct: The strip is 8 by 2, so 16 comes off: 784.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out the size of the strip that is cut away.

byKey.sam: You agreed with Sam, who took off the gap of 2. Each unit of the gap is a lot of 8, so 16 comes off.
byKey.one-lot: You took off one 8. 98 is two short of 100, so two lots of 8 come off.
byKey.added: You added the strip. 98 is below 100, so the strip is cut away.

explain.text: The gap is 2, but each unit of the gap is a whole lot of 8. So $8 \times 98 = 800 - 2 \times 8 = 784$. Pay back the gap times the other number, never the gap alone.

screens.prose: Every time, you went to a round number, then adjusted. For any whole number $n$, $$99n = 100n - n \qquad 5n = \frac{10n}{2} \qquad 25n = \frac{100n}{4}$$ Now give a reason for each line of $12 \times 25$.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $= \dfrac{600}{2}$, halve the top and the bottom

hints.text: Which line still has 25 in it?
Multiplying by 100 comes before any halving.
Rewrite 25, multiply by 100, then halve twice.

feedback.correct: Rewrite, multiply by 100, then halve twice.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the line that rewrites 25.

byKey.hundred: That line already has 1200 in it. First write 25 as a quarter of 100.
byKey.halve: Halving needs 1200 over 4 to work on. Multiply by 100 first.
byKey.again: That is the answer, so it comes last.

explain.text: Multiplying by 100 just adds two zeros. Dividing by 4 is two halvings: 1200, then 600, then 300. So $12 \times 25 = 300$.

screens.prose: A broker sells this stock in lots of 250 shares. You buy one lot at £12.00 a share. 250 is a quarter of 1,000.
screens.question: What is the lot worth, in pounds?

widget.label: Value of the lot in pounds

hints.text: One lot is the shaded quarter.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Price 1,000 shares, then take a quarter.

byKey.twenty-five: That prices 25 shares. A lot is 250, ten times as many.
byKey.halved-once: You halved once, which prices 500 shares. Halve again for 250.
byKey.no-quarter: That is 1,000 shares. One lot is a quarter of that.
byKey.hundred: That prices 100 shares. 250 shares is a quarter of 1,000.

explain.text: 1,000 shares at £12.00 cost £12,000. 250 is a quarter of 1,000, so the lot costs $12000 \div 4 = 3000$ pounds. The same move turns 25, 250 and 2,500 into quarters of 100, 1,000 and 10,000.

ideas: Round the multiplier, then pay back the gap in whole lots: $7 \times 99 = 700 - 7$.
The payback is the gap times the other number: $8 \times 98 = 800 - 16$, not $800 - 2$.
Five is half of ten and 25 is a quarter of 100: go round, then halve once or twice.
summary.trap: Taking off the gap instead of the gap in lots: $8 \times 98$ is $800 - 16 = 784$, not 798.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out 6 × 100, then take off one lot of 6.

byKey.one-not-lot: You took 1 off 600. One lot here is 6.
byKey.no-adjust: That is 6 × 100. One lot of 6 still has to come off.
byKey.added: You added a lot. 99 is below 100, so it comes off.

explain.text: $6 \times 100 = 600$, and one lot of 6 comes off. $600 - 6 = 594$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out 10 × 86, then halve it.

byKey.no-halve: That is ten lots of 86. Halve it for five lots.
byKey.lost-zero: You halved 86 but skipped the ten lots. Half of 860 is 430.
byKey.extra-zero: You went to 100 lots. Five is half of ten, not of 100.

explain.text: $10 \times 86 = 860$, and half of that is 430. So $5 \times 86 = 430$.

quiz.prose: You hold £6,400 of a stock. Your hedge ratio is 0.99, so you sell £0.99 of the index for every £1 of stock.
quiz.question: How much of the index do you sell, in pounds?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 0.99 is 1 less 0.01, so take 1% of £6,400 off £6,400.

byKey.one-not-lot: You took £1 off. The gap is 0.01 of every pound, so take off 1% of £6,400, which is £64.
byKey.ten-percent: You took off 10%. 0.99 is 0.01 below 1, so take off 1%: £64.
byKey.added: You added 1%. 0.99 is below 1, so the 1% comes off.

explain.text: $0.99 = 1 - 0.01$, so the hedge is $6400 - 0.01 \times 6400 = 6400 - 64$. That is £6,336.00. It is the ×99 move, scaled down by 100.

quiz.prose: 51 is just above a round number. Combine two moves from the lesson.
quiz.question: What is 8 × 51?

feedback.correct: Half of 800 is 400, and one more lot of 8 makes 408.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. 8 × 50 is half of 8 × 100. Then add one lot of 8.

byKey.one-not-lot: You added 1. 51 is one lot above 50, so add 8.
byKey.no-adjust: That is 8 × 50. One more lot of 8 goes on.
byKey.subtracted: You took a lot off. 51 is above 50, so the extra lot goes on.

explain.text: $8 \times 50$ is half of $8 \times 100$, so 400. 51 is one above 50, so one lot of 8 goes on. $400 + 8 = 408$.
